bullets: How sin x is built term by term: each new term bends the polynomial closer to sin x and widens the accurate interval around 0
slides.heading: Maclaurin series: sin x built term by term
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we build sin x term by term and watch each term widen the match around 0.

bullets: Describe the Maclaurin series for sin x: x - x^3/3! + x^5/5! - x^7/7! and so on
Explain why each added term widens the accurate interval around 0, yet no fixed polynomial matches sin x far from 0
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to build the series and judge where it can be trusted.

bullets: The flat line P = 0 touches sin x only at the origin
So how close can a polynomial get - and how far from 0 does the match last?
slides.heading: Matching only at 0 - for now?
slides.notes: Ask the class: the constant polynomial matches only at one point - what should we add first? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because each term has a job.

bullets: A Maclaurin series is a polynomial centred at 0, built from derivatives at 0
For sin x the terms alternate in sign: x, -x^3/3!, +x^5/5!, -x^7/7!, with odd powers only
Each term corrects the previous polynomial over a wider interval around 0, but every fixed polynomial eventually diverges from sin x
slides.heading: Terms centred at 0
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: judge a polynomial by its accurate interval around 0 first, because widening is not the same as matching everywhere.

bullets: The constant polynomial P = 0 is flat
It is exact only where it crosses sin x at the origin
slides.heading: The constant polynomial matches only at 0
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the origin marker: the flat line meets sin x only at that single point.

bullets: Adding x tilts the flat line into the diagonal y = x
It hugs sin x near 0 but peels away beyond a narrow band
slides.heading: Adding x: a narrow match near 0
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and watch the green band: name where the diagonal stays close and where it peels away.

bullets: Subtracting x^3/3! bends the diagonal into a cubic
The cubic follows sin x much further, so the accurate region visibly widens
slides.heading: The cubic term widens the accurate region
slides.notes: Play scene 3 slowly: follow the curve bending onto sin x and compare the band width with scene 2.

bullets: Adding x^5/5! makes the polynomial near-coincident with sin x over a wide band
Far from 0 even the quintic still separates from sin x
slides.heading: The quintic matches widely, but not everywhere
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and follow the far-field markers: watch the wide match near 0, then the visible gap at x = 3.

bullets: At x = 0.5 the cubic x - x^3/3! already gives about 0.479, close to sin 0.5
Adding x^5/5! improves it further near 0, while at x = 3 the same quintic is visibly off
slides.heading: Worked example: reading the widening
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, evaluate the linear term at small x - close to sin x. Step 2, add the cubic correction and see the match improve. Step 3, check x = 3: the quintic and sin x are still apart, so the interval matters.

bullets: In pairs: predict what the next term -x^7/7! does to the accurate interval, and where the match still fails
Then swap and check: did your partner widen the interval around 0 instead of claiming a global match?
slides.heading: Your turn: predict the next term
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for interval-first reasoning, then take two pairs answers: the septic term widens the accurate interval further around 0, but far from 0 the polynomial still breaks down.

bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who thinks extra terms fix the match at every x
Name the widening interval around 0 and the breakdown far from 0 to earn full credit
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers widen the interval instead of claiming a match everywhere.
